transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on what the fault turns out to be. If it is the drive belt, that is usually a simple, low-cost repair worth doing even on a 9-year-old machine. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drive belt [belt-driven machines ONLY]. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
I turned it by hand with the power off and it turns freely and quietly, no scraping or rumble. Nothing feels stiff or loose to me.
Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?

No, it doesn't spin at all when empty. It just sits there, and the drum doesn't move in the wash either. I did notice a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, though not since. Could that be related?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, it could be. A hot electrical smell followed by the drum not turning at all can point to something in the motor or its electrics having overheated, but there's no way to confirm that from the outside. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
